papers.title: Rado's covering problem for cubes and balls: a survey
papers.abstract: What is the largest constant $c\in [0,1]$ with the property that every finite collection $\mathcal{C}$ of axis-parallel squares in the plane admits a disjoint sub-collection $\mathcal{S}$ occupying at least a fraction $c$ of the area covered by $\mathcal{C}$? This problem was first raised by T.~Rad\'o in 1928, who was motivated by a classical covering lemma in real analysis due to Vitali. R.~Rado later generalized the problem from axis-parallel squares in the plane to homothetic copies of any given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where now we are looking for an optimal constant $F(K)$. In this paper we survey the literature on this problem, with a focus on the case where $K$ is a cube or a ball in the high-dimensional regime $d\rightarrow \infty$. The estimates that we currently have for cubes are much more precise than those for balls: namely if $Q^d$ is a $d$-dimensional cube, then \[ (e^{-1}+o(1))\frac{2^{-d}}{d \log{d}} \leq F(Q^d)\leq 2^{-d}, \] while denoting $B^d$ a $d$-dimensional Euclidean ball, then \[ 2.910^{-d} \leq F(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}.\] Except for the upper bound for cubes, which is classical, the other estimates are due to the authors.

papers.title: Sharp Fractional Capacitary-Distance Hardy Inequalities
papers.abstract: Let $d\in\mathbb N$, $p\in(1,\infty)$, $p':=\frac{p}{p-1}$, and $s\in(0,\min\{1+\frac1p,\frac dp\})$. For an open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, let $F:=\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\Omega$. For any $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $x\in\Omega$, let \begin{align*} d_{\alpha,s,p}(x) :=\inf\left\{r\in(0,\infty): \frac{\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{F\cap B(x,r)})} {\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{B(x,r)})}\ge\alpha\right\}, \end{align*} where $\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}$ is the capacity associated with the fractional Sobolev energy $[\,\cdot\,]_{s,p}^p$. In this article, we prove that there exists a positive constant $C$, depending only on $d$, $s$, and $p$, such that, for any $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $u\in C_{\rm c}^\infty(\Omega)$, \begin{align*} \int_\Omega\frac{|u(x)|^p}{d_{\alpha,s,p}(x)^{sp}}\,dx \le C\alpha^{-p'}[u]_{s,p}^p. \end{align*} We also show that both the exponent $p'$ in $\alpha^{-p'}$ as $\alpha\to0^+$ over the class of all open sets and the range $s\in(0,1+\frac1p)$ within $sp<d$ are sharp. Our proofs use variational minimization, equilibrium measures on trees, and weighted Hardy inequalities.

papers.title: Characterization of parabolic rectifiability in terms of Jones' square function
papers.abstract: We show that a measure $\mu$ in $\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic metric is rectifiable (in the parabolic sense) if and only if the Jones' square function is finite $\mu$-almost everywhere. This square function is constructed using the parabolic version of the Jones' beta numbers, which control how close $\mu$ is to being supported in time-independent planes (these planes are the paradigmatic example of parabolic rectifiable set). Our only background assumption is that $\mu$ has positive and finite densities (qualitatively) almost everywhere. A key feature of our proof is the use of a parabolic version of the Reifenberg parametrization theorem, which in the Euclidean setting is due to David and Toro (MAMS, 2012), and has recently been extended to the parabolic setting by Hoffman, Mourgoglou and the fourth author. In the latter work, the authors construct a bi-H\"older map. Here, under an additional summability condition, we improve this construction to obtain a parabolic regular bi-Lipschitz map. This improvement in regularity plays a crucial role in our arguments.

papers.title: Power loss for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi estimate on smooth hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove power-type lower bounds for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi constants for $C^{2,\beta}$ hypersurfaces with $0<\beta\leq1$ whose second fundamental form is nonzero at some point. This result, in particular, disproves the so-called local Mizohata--Takeuchi conjectures for the paraboloid and the sphere and, in turn, presents an obstruction to a general weighted approach to the theory of Fourier restriction of those classical surfaces.

papers.title: Sharp Weak-Type Inequalities for Scalar and Matrix Weights
papers.abstract: Let $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $p':=\frac p{p-1}$. In this article, we establish a mixed multiplier weak-type inequality with weight dependence $[w]_{A_p}^{\frac1p}[w]_{A_\infty}^{\max\{\frac1p,\frac1{p'}\}}$ for scalar $A_p$ weights and Calder\'on--Zygmund operators whose modulus of continuity satisfies the Dini condition. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp exponent $\max\{1,\frac2p\}$ of $[w]_{A_p}$ in the corresponding pure $A_p$ bound. Moreover, in the matrix-weighted setting, we prove the sharpness of the exponent $1+\min\{\frac1p,\frac1{p(p-1)}\}$ of $[W]_{\mathcal A_p}$ in the known multiplier weak-type inequality for the Hilbert transform.

papers.title: The weak-type (1,1) bound for the Hardy--Littlewood maximal function is $O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$
papers.abstract: We prove a weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal function with respect to Euclidean balls with dimensional dependence $O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$. This improves the order of growth in the classical $O(n)$ estimate of Stein and Str\"omberg. The proof goes through a pointwise bound of the Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator by the heat maximal operator with $\sqrt{n}$ loss. The key technical aspect of our result is an improvement of the weak-type bound for the heat maximal operator from $O(\sqrt{n})$ to $O(\log n)$.

papers.title: Pinned simplex volumes from thin sets in Euclidean spaces
papers.abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a Borel set, with $d\geq2$. We prove that if $\dim_{\mathrm H}(E)>d/2$, then there exist distinct points $a,b\in E$ such that the set of triangle areas with fixed base $a,b$ and third vertex varying in $E$ has positive Lebesgue measure. More generally, for $2\leq r\leq d$, if \[ \dim_{\mathrm H}(E)> \max\left\{r-1,\frac{d-r+2}{2}\right\}, \] then there are $r$ affinely independent points in $E$ for which the corresponding base-pinned $r$-simplex volume set has positive Lebesgue measure. The geometric input is a thin-plane estimate of Bright, Ortiz, and Zakharov \cite{BrightOrtizZakharov}. For a suitable $(r-2)$-dimensional anchor spanned by $E$, this estimate yields simultaneous Frostman bounds for a projected vertex measure in the normal space of the anchor and for the distribution of directions determining bases that share the anchor. The Peres--Schlag machinery \cite{PeresSchlag}, applied to a local family of distance-to-line maps in this $(d-r+2)$-dimensional normal space, then produces the desired base. Finally, we establish an exact correspondence between fixed-base simplex volumes and pinned distances in the normal space of the base, prove a converse for matched bases in layered lifts, and obtain the lower obstruction $\max\{r-1,d/(2r)\}$ for any universal dimension threshold.

papers.title: A counterexample to the one-supremum conjecture and sharp logarithmic weighted bounds for Calder\'on--Zygmund operators
papers.abstract: We give a negative answer to the one-supremum conjecture of Hyt\"onen and Lacey~\cite[Remark~1.3]{HL}, in the strong-type form stated by Lerner and Moen~\cite[Conjecture~1.3, formula~(9)]{LM}. The conjecture asks whether the mixed $A_p$--$A_\infty$ characteristics $K_p(w)$ and $K_{p'}(\sigma)$, with both factors evaluated on the same cube, control Calder\'on--Zygmund operators without a logarithmic loss. For every $1<p<\infty$, we construct explicit weights for which $K_p(w)+K_{p'}(\sigma)\eqsim_p m$, but one fixed Hilbert transform has weighted norm at least $m(1+\log m)^{\gamma_p}$, where $\gamma_p=\max\{1/p,1/p'\}$. Thus the proposed bound fails even for a fixed singular integral. The counterexample also extends to a fixed Riesz transform in each dimension $n\ge2$. We further establish a logarithmically corrected bound for Calder\'on--Zygmund operators, with powers $1/p'$ and $1/p$ on the respective one-supremum terms. Together, the lower and upper bounds identify $\gamma_p$ as the optimal common logarithmic exponent and give the sharp worst-case growth $(1+\log A)^{\gamma_p}$ under the constraint $[w]_{A_p}\le A$. The results show why information from any one cube cannot fully capture the accumulation of a singular integral across many scales.

papers.title: Global existence and emergent dynamics of singular Cucker-Smale model on general digraphs
papers.abstract: We investigate the global-in-time dynamics of the Cucker--Smale model under general network topologies with a singular communication weight function $\psi(r) = r^{-\alpha}$, $\alpha>0$. For $\alpha \ge 1$, we establish the global-in-time existence of smooth solutions when network topologies belong to one of several classes of directed graphs. In particular, in one dimension, we present a necessary condition on the network topology for global existence by constructing finite-time blow-up solutions from non-collisional initial configurations. Moreover, we provide a sufficient framework for the emergence of mono-cluster flocking. For certain classes of network topologies, we further show that mono-cluster flocking occurs unconditionally for non-collisional initial configuration when $\alpha =1$.

papers.title: Subharmonic functions and convexity of the Radon transform, with applications to the Fourier transform
papers.abstract: Integrating a subharmonic function over parallel hyperplanes produces a convex function of the signed distance from the origin, provided that the function is absolutely integrable on bounded slabs. We prove this first for twice continuously differentiable functions and then without any smoothness assumption, and the same argument applies to a function defined only on a slab. Examples on the disk explain why subharmonicity on a bounded convex domain does not imply convexity of the integrals over its chords. We then apply a one-dimensional Fourier representation for convex functions to the Radon transform, which leads to a directional formula for integrable subharmonic functions on slabs. For functions on bounded convex domains whose Radon transforms are convex, we obtain a weighted estimate for the integral of the Fourier transform in terms of boundary layers and the gradient.

papers.title: Another Variant of the Neoclassical Inequality
papers.abstract: The neoclassical inequality is an inequality related to the binomial theorem, involving fractional powers. It naturally gives rise to four other similar inequalities, by varying the inequality sign and the range of the fractional parameter. Three of these statements are known, and the remaining one was conjectured in the literature, based on numerical evidence. It is proved in the present note. The method we use yields short proofs for two of the known related inequalities.

papers.title: Round hyperspheres uniquely minimize most tangent-point energies
papers.abstract: We show that round hyperspheres uniquely minimize a broad class of generalized tangent-point energies among all boundaries of bounded Caccioppoli sets sharing the same perimeter or enclosed volume. This includes closed $C^1$-hypersurfaces. Equivalently, we establish sharp lower bounds for the associated scale-invariant ratios of energy to surface measure and energy to volume, respectively, with equality precisely for round spheres.

papers.title: Circular Vector Tomography with Partial Radial Data
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce and study several generalized circular Radon transforms acting on smooth vector fields compactly supported in a planar annulus, with centers restricted to the outer acquisition circle and truncated measurement radii. The operators of interest are the longitudinal and transverse circular Radon transforms and their weighted analogues. We characterize the kernels of the individual unweighted transforms. Then we establish the reconstruction of a vector field from the combined longitudinal and transverse circular Radon transform data. We further show that the pairs formed by each transform and its weighted analogue is not sufficient for the complete recovery of a vector field. However, we demonstrate that full reconstruction is possible with suitable additional data. Finally, we numerically implement and validate the derived inversion formulas.

papers.title: On the multiplicity of crossing limit cycles of double diagonalizable piecewise linear vector fields
papers.abstract: We consider planar piecewise linear vector fields with two zones separated by a straight line and having two diagonalizable components, which we call the \emph{double diagonalizable configuration}. In this configuration, the Poincar\'{e} half-maps correspond to separatrices of saddle points in the foliations of symmetric differential forms $\omega_r(x)-\omega_r(y)$, where $\omega_r$ is a rational $1$-form with exactly three simple poles. Limit cycles correspond to non-diagonal intersections of two such separatrices, and the multiplicity of a limit cycle is precisely the order of contact at the intersection point. We prove that two distinct separatrices which are not nested segments of the same straight line have a contact of order at most $4$ at a diagonal point and at most $2$ at a non-diagonal point. As a consequence, we obtain that the multiplicity of limit cycles in the double diagonalizable configuration is at most two, this bound being sharp.

papers.title: $\ell^p$-Improving for Discrete Fractional Integrals and Averages on the Moment Curve
papers.abstract: We prove the $\ell^p$-improving estimates in the full range for discrete fractional integral operators on the moment curve (except at the endpoint) and discrete averages on the moment curve (with $N^{\epsilon}$-losses). This follows via essentially sharp Diophantine solution counting estimates for inhomogeneous Vinogradov systems with an odd number of variables.

papers.title: Boundary Feller-Dynkin processes associated with Laguerre processes and Pickrell diffusions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a Feller-Dynkin boundary process by applying the method of intertwiners to the coherent family, introduced in our previous work, of Laguerre processes with a fixed parameter. The corresponding boundary process is computed explicitly, and it turns out to be a deterministic dynamical system. Since the Pickrell diffusions that leave the Pickrell measure invariant are coherent with respect to the same projective system, we also obtain the stochastic boundary process associated with the coherent family of Pickrell diffusions.

papers.title: Liouville regular Jordan curves
papers.abstract: We investigate Liouville regular Jordan curves, which were introduced in our previous paper as "Jordan curves that admit continuous Legendrian lifts". We prove that a Jordan curve satisfying certain variation conditions in a neighborhood of each point is Liouville regular. We also prove that the boundary of a Jordan domain is Liouville regular if the images of the radial tails under a conformal mapping have uniformly vanishing length. Together with our previous result, these criteria show that each such Jordan curve admits an inscribed rectangle in every prescribed similarity class.

papers.title: Weak Hurwitz stability of extended Tur\'an expressions for Stirling--Whitney--Riordan and Laguerre polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a sufficient condition for weak Hurwitz stability of extended Tur\'an expressions associated with polynomial sequences satisfying a first-order differential recurrence. As applications, we prove weak Hurwitz stability of extended Tur\'an expressions for the Stirling--Whitney--Riordan polynomials, several families of Eulerian polynomials, the Bell polynomials, and the reflected generalized Laguerre polynomials. These results settle two conjectures of Chasse, Grabarek, and Visontai concerning the Bell and Laguerre polynomials.

papers.title: A resolution of the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem in the large
papers.abstract: We show that for every unbounded set $A\subset\mathbb R$ and every $0<\varepsilon<1$, there exists a closed set $S\subset\mathbb R$ that has measure at least $1-\varepsilon$ in every unit interval and contains no nontrivial affine copy of $A$. Moreover, $S$ can be chosen so that $|S\cap[x,x+1]|\to1$ as $|x|\to\infty$. This resolves the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem in the large.
